title: Managing Secrets and Credentials
subtopics: Keeping credentials out of source control
learning_outcomes: Explain the role of managing secrets and credentials in a Ruby program and name the key rule involved.
Apply managing secrets and credentials in a small example and predict its result before running it.
Identify one boundary or failure case related to secure deployment configuration and verify the intended behavior.

content.intro: Learn Managing Secrets and Credentials through a visual model, a minimal Ruby example, and a practical check.
content.why_it_matters: Understanding managing secrets and credentials helps you write code that is easier to explain, test, and maintain. It also helps separate Ruby language guarantees from runtime assumptions, dependency behavior, and application-specific rules.

content_blocks.title: The core idea
content_blocks.text: Managing Secrets and Credentials helps you reason about environment-based configuration. In Ruby, prefer a small example whose inputs and expected result are easy to explain. This lesson connects the syllabus topic to practical code and highlights where assumptions or edge cases matter.

content_blocks.title: How to think about it
content_blocks.text: Begin by identifying the key rule: Environment-based configuration. Then connect it to Keeping credentials out of source control. The remaining syllabus points—Credential rotation, Secure deployment configuration—are useful checks before applying this in a larger project.

content_blocks.title: Guided example
content_blocks.text: Run the example as written, compare it with the expected result, and explain why each line supports managing secrets and credentials. Next change one input or condition and predict the result before running it.

content_blocks.title: Run, troubleshoot, and reset
content_blocks.text: Save as lesson.rb and run `ruby lesson.rb` from a terminal. CodeLeaf currently has no isolated Ruby runner, so these examples should be run locally until one is deployed. Reset by removing temporary files created by your experiment and returning the code to the smallest reproducible example.

content_blocks.title: Recap
content_blocks.text: You should now be able to explain managing secrets and credentials, identify its place in ruby application security, run a focused example, and verify an important boundary. Revisit the linked exercise if this is a core topic; advanced runtime or framework examples remain draft until reviewed in a suitable environment.
